heading: Cold open
narration: Add enough chromium to iron and a film too thin to see stops rust.

heading: Cold open
narration: You keep steel from rusting by denying the reaction one of its ingredients: seal water and oxygen away with a coating, alloy the steel with at least 10.5 percent chromium so it grows its own protective oxide, or let a more reactive metal such as zinc corrode in its place.

heading: Cold open
narration: That chromium threshold is the usual definition of stainless steel, as ASM International sets it out.

heading: Cold open
narration: But a threshold is not a promise. Stainless steel left in salt spray can still pit, and a painted girder can rust from a scratch you cannot see.

heading: Cold open
narration: What the figure settles is chemistry. What it leaves open is time, environment and care.

heading: Title card
narration: How do you keep steel from rusting?

heading: Rust is an electrical circuit running across a wet surface
narration: Start with what rust actually is. When iron sits under a film of water, some spots on the surface give up electrons, and the iron there dissolves as ions.

heading: Rust is an electrical circuit running across a wet surface
narration: Those spots are the anode. The electrons travel through the metal to other spots, the cathode, where oxygen dissolved in the water picks them up.

heading: Rust is an electrical circuit running across a wet surface
narration: The water itself is the electrolyte. It carries ions between the two sites, so the circuit closes.

heading: Rust is an electrical circuit running across a wet surface
narration: Where the dissolved iron meets the products of the oxygen reaction, they combine into hydrated iron oxides. That reddish-brown material is rust.

heading: Rust is an electrical circuit running across a wet surface
narration: Rust is an electrochemical reaction, not simple contact between iron and air, and that is known from experiment rather than assumed.

heading: Rust is an electrical circuit running across a wet surface
narration: Corrosion scientists can separate the two halves of the reaction, hold a sample at a controlled electrical potential, and measure the current that flows.

heading: Rust is an electrical circuit running across a wet surface
narration: The results line up with what you see outdoors. Dry air causes very little rusting.

heading: Rust is an electrical circuit running across a wet surface
narration: Water with the oxygen removed causes very little. Put water, oxygen and something that carries ions together, especially dissolved salt, and the rate climbs.

heading: Rust is an electrical circuit running across a wet surface
narration: That is why a car driven on salted winter roads, or parked by the sea, rusts faster than the same car kept in a dry garage.

heading: Rust fails as armour where other oxides succeed
narration: Many metals oxidise. What matters is what the oxide does next. Aluminium forms a skin of oxide almost instantly, and that skin clings to the metal and seals it.

args.meaning: a thin, tight oxide layer that slows further reaction
args.boundary: rust is porous and flakes away

heading: Rust fails as armour where other oxides succeed
narration: Metallurgists call a protective oxide like that a passive film: a thin, tight oxide layer that slows further reaction.

heading: Rust fails as armour where other oxides succeed
narration: Rust behaves differently. It takes up more space than the iron it came from, it holds water, and rust is porous and flakes away.

heading: Rust fails as armour where other oxides succeed
narration: Each flake exposes fresh metal underneath, so the reaction never runs out of surface to attack.

heading: Rust fails as armour where other oxides succeed
narration: That is the core problem every protection method is trying to solve.

args.meaning: a thin, tight oxide layer that slows further reaction
args.boundary: rust is porous and flakes away

heading: Rust fails as armour where other oxides succeed
narration: You either keep the electrolyte away from the iron, change the iron so its oxide behaves more like aluminium's, or change which metal gives up electrons.

heading: Rust fails as armour where other oxides succeed
narration: Call them barrier, alloy and sacrifice. Each one is a different way to interrupt the circuit.

heading: Producer POV
narration: A warning was dismissed. Maintenance was delayed. Somebody normalised a problem because nothing terrible happened the first ten times.

args.text: A warning was dismissed. Maintenance was delayed. Somebody normalised a problem because nothing terrible happened the first ten times.

heading: A coating protects only while it stays unbroken
narration: The oldest strategy is the barrier. Paint, oil, wax, powder coat and polymer films all work the same way: they keep water and oxygen off the steel.

heading: A coating protects only while it stays unbroken
narration: A coating is a barrier against water and oxygen, not a cure for rust already started.

heading: A coating protects only while it stays unbroken
narration: Paint brushed over existing rust traps moisture against the metal, which is why surface preparation matters as much as the paint itself: removing rust and mill scale, and roughening the surface so the coating grips.

includes: a barrier against water and oxygen
excludes: a cure for rust already started

heading: A coating protects only while it stays unbroken
narration: Even a good coating is slightly permeable. Water slowly diffuses through most organic films, so serious coating systems stack layers.

heading: A coating protects only while it stays unbroken
narration: A primer bonds to the steel and often carries corrosion inhibitors, intermediate coats add thickness, and a topcoat resists sunlight and abrasion.

includes: a barrier against water and oxygen
excludes: a cure for rust already started

heading: A coating protects only while it stays unbroken
narration: The weakness of any barrier is the breach. A stone chip or a scratch exposes a small patch of steel, and the circuit restarts there.

heading: A coating protects only while it stays unbroken
narration: Rust can then creep sideways under the paint, lifting the film from beneath, so the visible blister is often smaller than the damage.

heading: A coating protects only while it stays unbroken
narration: That is why inspectors of painted structures look first at edges, welds, bolt holes and places where water pools, rather than at the broad flat faces that look fine.

heading: Zinc protects steel by corroding first
narration: The sacrificial strategy is stranger, because it keeps working where the coating is broken.

heading: Zinc protects steel by corroding first
narration: Zinc is more reactive than iron. When zinc and steel touch in the same electrolyte, zinc gives up electrons more readily, so the zinc becomes the anode and steel becomes the cathode.

heading: Zinc protects steel by corroding first
narration: The zinc corrodes, and the steel is spared. This is galvanizing. In hot-dip galvanizing, cleaned steel is dipped in molten zinc, which bonds metallurgically to the surface as layers of zinc-iron alloy topped with nearly pure zinc.

heading: Zinc protects steel by corroding first
narration: A scratch through that layer does not start rust the way a scratch through paint does, because the surrounding zinc keeps supplying electrons to the exposed steel.

heading: Zinc protects steel by corroding first
narration: This is not a niche technique. USGS, the United States Geological Survey, which tracks mineral commodities, reports that galvanizing is a leading use of zinc.

heading: Zinc protects steel by corroding first
narration: ASTM International publishes standards for galvanized coatings, setting how much zinc different products must carry.

heading: Zinc protects steel by corroding first
narration: The same principle scales up. Ship hulls, buried pipelines and offshore platforms carry blocks of zinc, aluminium or magnesium alloys bolted on as sacrificial anodes, and those blocks are replaced as they waste away.

heading: Zinc protects steel by corroding first
narration: Some large structures use impressed current instead: a power supply pushes electrons onto the steel so it stays the cathode.

heading: Zinc protects steel by corroding first
narration: Either way, the protection is consumed. A sacrificial anode that is never replaced eventually protects nothing.

heading: Stainless steel heals itself, until chlorides break through
narration: The alloy strategy changes the steel itself. Add chromium, and the chromium at the surface reacts with oxygen to form a passive film of chromium oxide only a few nanometres thick.

heading: Stainless steel heals itself, until chlorides break through
narration: The usual definition of stainless steel, as ASM International describes it, is at least 10.5 percent chromium by mass.

heading: Stainless steel heals itself, until chlorides break through
narration: Below that level the film is not reliably continuous. Above it, the film forms and, critically, repairs itself.

heading: Stainless steel heals itself, until chlorides break through
narration: Scratch stainless steel in air and the exposed chromium reoxidises, sealing the wound.

heading: Stainless steel heals itself, until chlorides break through
narration: That self-healing behaviour, not hardness or shine, is what the word stainless really describes.

heading: Stainless steel heals itself, until chlorides break through
narration: Stainless steel is stain-resistant, not stain-proof. The passive film needs oxygen to repair itself, and chloride ions, from seawater, road salt or some cleaning products, attack it at weak points.

heading: Stainless steel heals itself, until chlorides break through
narration: The result is pitting: small, deep holes that can penetrate a part while most of the surface still looks bright.

heading: Stainless steel heals itself, until chlorides break through
narration: Crevices are worse, because a narrow gap starves the repair of oxygen while chlorides concentrate inside.

heading: Stainless steel heals itself, until chlorides break through
narration: Grades meant for marine service add molybdenum, which makes the passive film more resistant to chloride attack.

heading: Stainless steel heals itself, until chlorides break through
narration: Choosing a stainless grade is a judgement about environment, not a single yes-or-no property.

heading: Stainless steel heals itself, until chlorides break through
narration: Weathering steel takes a middle path. Small additions of copper, chromium and other elements make its rust form a denser, more adherent layer that slows further attack.

heading: Stainless steel heals itself, until chlorides break through
narration: But that layer only develops where the surface regularly dries out. Kept permanently wet, weathering steel simply rusts.

heading: Corrosion rates are measured, not assumed
narration: Everything so far rests on measurement, and it helps to know which kind.

heading: Corrosion rates are measured, not assumed
narration: The simplest method is the coupon, a small flat sample of the metal.

heading: Corrosion rates are measured, not assumed
narration: You weigh the coupon, expose it on a rack at a test site or in a tank, strip the rust chemically, and weigh again.

heading: Corrosion rates are measured, not assumed
narration: The difference, divided by the exposed area and the time, gives metal lost per year.

heading: Corrosion rates are measured, not assumed
narration: Exposure sites in industrial, coastal and rural settings run these racks for years, because the atmosphere cannot be hurried.

heading: Corrosion rates are measured, not assumed
narration: The faster route uses the circuit itself. Place a sample in an electrolyte, control its potential, and measure the current.

heading: Corrosion rates are measured, not assumed
narration: Current is a flow of electrons, and every electron released corresponds to iron dissolving, so the current converts directly into a corrosion rate in hours rather than years.

heading: Corrosion rates are measured, not assumed
narration: Laboratories including NIST have long studied how to make corrosion measurements like these reliable and comparable.

heading: Salt fog ranks coatings but cannot tell you how long they will last
narration: Manufacturers cannot wait years to qualify a new paint, so they use accelerated tests.

heading: Salt fog ranks coatings but cannot tell you how long they will last
narration: Panels sit in a closed cabinet in a continuous warm fog of salt water, and inspectors record when blisters, creep from a scribed line, or red rust appear.

heading: Salt fog ranks coatings but cannot tell you how long they will last
narration: Real exposure alternates wet and dry, sun and shade, and zinc layers and many coatings depend on those dry spells to form stable corrosion products.

heading: Salt fog ranks coatings but cannot tell you how long they will last
narration: A constant fog can rank two systems in the wrong order. Cyclic tests, which alternate spray, humidity and drying, were developed to narrow that gap, and engineers still check them against outdoor racks.

heading: What to notice in the edit
narration: When the close-up footage of scratched panels appears, watch the scribed line rather than the open face.

heading: What to notice in the edit
narration: On the painted panel, rust spreads sideways beneath the film. On the galvanized panel, the scratch stays grey for longer, because zinc around it is doing the corroding.

heading: What to notice in the edit
narration: On the stainless sample, look for isolated dark specks rather than a general bloom.

heading: What to notice in the edit
narration: Those specks are pits, and they are the reason a bright surface can still hide a failing part.

heading: Evidence limit
narration: Laboratory chemistry has settled the mechanism, and decades of exposure racks have settled the broad ranking of methods.

heading: Evidence limit
narration: What this evidence does not establish is service life at a given site.

heading: Evidence limit
narration: Corrosion rate depends on how often a surface stays wet, how much salt or pollution reaches it, whether water pools in a joint, and how well a coating was applied on one particular day.

heading: Evidence limit
narration: A test cabinet cannot reproduce all of that, and published exposure data describe the sites where racks stood, not your bridge, railing or boat trailer.

heading: Evidence limit
narration: For any real structure, the honest answer combines the right method with inspection over time.

heading: Closing
narration: Rust is patient. It needs only iron, water and oxygen, and it waits for the one scratch, crevice or neglected joint where all three meet.

heading: Closing
narration: Every method that stops it is a way of standing between those ingredients, and every one of them works only as long as someone keeps it standing.
